name: Vawksa Rep
ingredients: 500g pork belly, cut into 2-inch chunks (skin on)
1 cup fermented bamboo shoots (tuai), rinsed and drained
1 head garlic, cloves separated and smashed
2 tablespoons mustard oil (or any vegetable oil)
2 cups bamboo leaves (for wrapping, or use banana leaves)
instructions: 1. Marinate the pork with turmeric and salt for 30 minutes.
2. In a heavy-bottomed pan, heat mustard oil until smoking. Add pork chunks and sear on all sides until browned. Remove and set aside.
3. In the same oil, sauté onions, garlic, ginger, and green chilies until fragrant and onions are translucent.
4. Add the fermented bamboo shoots and cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
5. Return the pork to the pan, add water, and bring to a boil. Cover and simmer on low heat for 45 minutes, or until pork is tender. Check seasoning.
6. Preheat a tandoor or oven to 200°C (400°F). Line a baking dish with bamboo leaves. Transfer the pork mixture onto the leaves, fold the leaves to enclose, and secure with kitchen twine.
7. Place the wrapped packet in the oven and bake for 15-20 minutes, until the leaves are charred and fragrant.
8. Remove from oven, let rest for 5 minutes, then unwrap and serve hot with steamed rice.
description: A smoky, heart-warming embrace of fermented bamboo and mountain herbs.
